text:
Sophia: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a tiny 'contract envelope' as a canonical translation layer between the public API surface and hosting adapters (hosted / dedicated / private). Goal: reduce duplicated manifest logic, make fallbacks and capabilities explicit, and centralize versioning. High-level: small JSON schema + adapter translation hooks. Comments?

Ryan: Sounds promising. How is this different from the various manifest shapes we already have for each hosting mode? Also worried about extra translation adding request latency.

Sophia: Good Q. Difference is that current manifests diverged per-mode. Envelope would be a single, minimal superset: fields like capabilities, auth_modes, fallback_chain, telemetry_labels. Translation happens at deploy/load time inside the adapter, not per-request, so latency impact should be negligible.

Akshay: Two immediate concerns: (1) rollout / backward compatibility for existing Dedicated customers, (2) secret surface differences (KMS/HSM integrations) between Private and Hosted. Can we allow per-deployment overrides so we don't force a one-size-fits-all behavior?

Leah: Agree on overrides. Envelope should be a superset and allow an optional "overrides" map that adapters can honor. Also need schema versioning and a clear migration path when we change the envelope.

Maria: Observability angle — we need a consistent mapping to Redwood Console tags. Recommend adding an explicit "telemetry_key" + canonical labels in the envelope so adapters emit identical metrics. Also flag for dataflow constraints (GDPR/PII) so Console can filter.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Proposal pushed to infra RFC repo: https://git.internal/redwood/rfcs/contract-envelope. Added manifest-schema.yaml and basic CI validation.

Ryan: Implementation suggestion: POC inside runtime config loader: parse envelope -> produce canonical capability struct -> hand to serving layer. Keep a feature flag "use_contract_envelope" for at least 3 months and default off. We'll need adapter patches for hosted + one dedicated customer.

Sophia: Draft rollout plan: 1) Spec + schema + tests, 2) POC adapters for hosted and a dedicated pilot, 3) internal canary on low-traffic routes, 4) enable for new deployments behind flag, 5) provide migration tool for legacy manifests. @Akshay can you coordinate the dedicated pilot and legal checks?

Akshay: Yup — I'll coordinate with GTM and Legal on pilot terms and privacy considerations. Need a reliable rollback path and a test harness for secret passthroughs.

Leah: Add to RFC test checklist: schema roundtrip, override precedence tests, telemetry label correctness, secret-ref reference passthrough. Also include a perf benchmark to ensure manifest load stays < 1ms on cold start.

Maria: :thumbsup: Please include an explicit opt-out for on-prem private installs (we shouldn't auto-migrate air-gapped customers).

Sophia: Will update the RFC with the notes above and a minimal example schema. If there are no objections by EOD Friday I'll merge the spec and open the POC PRs. Thanks!
__notes: This thread captures a concise architecture sync about introducing a canonical contract envelope to unify manifests across hosting modes. Messages are ordered chronologically and follow Slack style.
